title: Deliveries Within a Time Budget
real_world_story: A delivery driver has a limited number of working hours and must finish as many deliveries as possible. Each delivery has a known service time. The dispatcher wants to know the maximum number of deliveries the driver can complete within a maximum time budget. Because the feasibility of a count is monotonic, the answer can be found efficiently with binary search.

real_world_connection.system: Capacity planning under a time budget
real_world_connection.input_represents: Deliveries as service times that consume the budget
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Binary searching on the answer to find the maximum feasible number of deliveries

problem_statement: Given N delivery service times and a maximum time budget B, determine the maximum number of deliveries that can be completed such that the sum of the selected service times is at most B.
task: Find the maximum number of deliveries that fit within the time budget.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and B, where N is the number of deliveries and B is the maximum time budget. The second line contains N integers representing the service time of each delivery.
output_format: Print the maximum number of deliveries that can be completed within the time budget.

examples.explanation: Sorted service times are 200, 300, 500, 700, 900. The two shortest, 200 + 300 = 500, fit within the budget of 600, but adding any third delivery would exceed it, so the maximum is 2.

expected_algorithm.name: Binary Search on Answer
expected_algorithm.reason: The maximum number of deliveries that fits the budget can be found by binary searching on the count, using the sorted service times to check feasibility.

hint: Sort the deliveries by service time so the shortest ones are considered first.
To check a count X, test whether the sum of the X smallest service times is at most B.
Because this check is monotonic, binary search over X finds the maximum feasible count.
real_world_takeaway: Binary Search on Answer lets a delivery company quickly decide how many deliveries fit within a driver's time budget, helping plan daily capacity.
